incidente.resumo: A configuration update incorrectly removed the minimum healthy hosts setting for the EC2 DNS resolver fleet in the Seoul (AP-NORTHEAST-2) Region, so it was interpreted as a very low default and DNS queries from within EC2 instances began to fail. Service was restored after further host removal was prevented and capacity was restored to previous levels.

descricao.texto: At 8:21 AM KST the engineering team was alerted to the DNS resolution issue in the AP-NORTHEAST-2 Region.
trechos: At 8:21 AM KST, the engineering team was alerted to the DNS resolution issue within the AP-NORTHEAST-2 Region and immediately began working on resolution.

descricao.texto: A configuration update incorrectly removed the setting that specifies the minimum healthy hosts for the EC2 DNS resolver fleet in AP-NORTHEAST-2; the setting was interpreted as a very low default value, resulting in fewer in-service healthy hosts, and with the reduced capacity DNS queries from within EC2 instances began to fail.
trechos: The root cause of DNS resolution issues was a configuration update which incorrectly removed the setting that specifies the minimum healthy hosts for the EC2 DNS resolver fleet in the AP-NORTHEAST-2 Region.
This resulted in the minimum healthy hosts configuration setting being interpreted as a very low default value that resulted in fewer in-service healthy hosts.
With the reduced healthy host capacity for the EC2 DNS resolver fleet, DNS queries from within EC2 instances began to fail.

descricao.texto: A configuration update removed the minimum healthy hosts setting of the EC2 DNS resolver fleet in the AP-NORTHEAST-2 Region.
trechos: The root cause of DNS resolution issues was a configuration update which incorrectly removed the setting that specifies the minimum healthy hosts for the EC2 DNS resolver fleet in the AP-NORTHEAST-2 Region.

passos.texto: After identifying the root cause at 8:48 AM KST, the team prevented additional healthy hosts from being removed from service, which took an additional 15 minutes.
trechos: We identified root cause at 8:48 AM KST and we first ensured that there was no further impact by preventing additional healthy hosts from being removed from service; this took an additional 15 minutes.

passos.texto: The team then restored the EC2 DNS resolver fleet's healthy host capacity to previous levels, which took the bulk of the recovery time; service was restored when the number of healthy hosts was restored, with full recovery at 9:43 AM KST.
trechos: We then started restoring capacity to previous levels which took the bulk of the recovery time.
Service was restored when the number of healthy hosts was restored to previous levels.
At 9:43 AM KST, DNS queries from within EC2 instances saw full recovery.

acoes.texto: Already done: validated that every AWS region has the correct capacity settings for the EC2 DNS resolver service.
trechos: We have immediately validated and ensured that every AWS region has the correct capacity settings for the EC2 DNS resolver service.

acoes.texto: Implementing semantic configuration validation for all EC2 DNS resolver configuration updates, to ensure every region always has sufficient minimum healthy hosts.
trechos: We are implementing semantic configuration validation for all EC2 DNS resolver configuration updates, to ensure every region always has sufficient minimum healthy hosts.

acoes.texto: Adding throttling so that only a limited amount of healthy host capacity can be removed from service each hour, intended to prevent downscaling of the EC2 DNS resolver fleet in the event of an invalid configuration parameter.
trechos: We are also adding throttling to ensure that only a limited amount of healthy host capacity can be removed from service each hour.
This will prevent the downscaling of the EC2 DNS resolver fleet in the event of an invalid configuration parameter.
Between 8:19 AM and 9:43 AM KST, EC2 instances experienced DNS resolution issues in the AP-NORTHEAST-2 region.
